heading.en: A cotton plant that makes its own pesticide

hook.en: Bollworms once forced cotton farmers to spray pesticide again and again. Bt cotton carries a bacterial gene, so the plant itself poisons the worm that bites it.

narration.en: Bollworms once forced cotton farmers to spray pesticide again and again. Bt cotton carries a bacterial gene, so the plant itself poisons the worm that bites it.
narration.kn: ಕಾಯಿಕೊರಕ ಹುಳುಗಳಿಂದಾಗಿ ಹತ್ತಿ ರೈತರು ಮತ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ಕೀಟನಾಶಕ ಸಿಂಪಡಿಸಬೇಕಾಗುತ್ತಿತ್ತು. Bt ಹತ್ತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಜೀನ್ ಇರುವುದರಿಂದ ಕಚ್ಚುವ ಹುಳುವಿಗೆ ಗಿಡವೇ ವಿಷವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Plants, bacteria, fungi and animals whose genes have been altered by manipulation are called genetically modified organisms (GMOs). GM plants have been useful in many ways: they are more tolerant to abiotic stresses (cold, drought, salt, heat); they reduce reliance on chemical pesticides (pest-resistant crops); they help reduce post-harvest losses; they increase the efficiency of mineral usage by plants, which prevents early exhaustion of soil fertility; and they enhance nutritional value of food, for example golden rice, which is rich in vitamin A. GM is also used to create tailor-made plants that supply alternative resources such as starches, fuels and pharmaceuticals to industry.

points.en: Better mineral use; golden rice rich in vitamin A

narration.en: Genetically modified crops can tolerate drought, salt and cold, need fewer pesticides, lose less after harvest, use minerals better and can be more nutritious, like vitamin A-rich golden rice.
narration.kn: ಕುಲಾಂತರಿ ಬೆಳೆಗಳು ಬರ, ಲವಣ, ಚಳಿ ಸಹಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ಕಡಿಮೆ ಕೀಟನಾಶಕ ಬೇಡುತ್ತವೆ, ಕೊಯ್ಲಿನ ನಂತರದ ನಷ್ಟ ತಗ್ಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ಖನಿಜಗಳನ್ನು ಉತ್ತಮವಾಗಿ ಬಳಸುತ್ತವೆ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಟಮಿನ್ A ಸಮೃದ್ಧ ಗೋಲ್ಡನ್ ರೈಸ್‌ನಂತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಪೌಷ್ಟಿಕವಾಗಬಹುದು.

body.en: Bt toxin is produced by the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt for short). Some strains form protein crystals during a particular phase of growth that are toxic to certain insects: lepidopterans (tobacco budworm, armyworm), coleopterans (beetles) and dipterans (flies, mosquitoes). The toxin exists as an inactive protoxin, so it does not kill the bacterium. Once an insect eats it, the alkaline pH of the gut solubilises the crystals and converts the protoxin into the active toxin. The active toxin binds to the surface of the midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, which cause the cells to swell and lyse, and the insect dies. The toxin is coded by genes named cry. The proteins coded by cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms, and that of cryIAb controls corn borer. The gene from B. thuringiensis has been put into crops such as cotton, corn, rice, tomato, potato and soybean.

points.en: Inactive protoxin → active toxin in the alkaline insect gut
Toxin makes pores in midgut epithelial cells → swelling, lysis, death

narration.en: Bacillus thuringiensis makes an inactive protoxin. In the alkaline gut of an insect it becomes active, punches pores in the midgut lining and kills the larva. cryIAc and cryIIAb protect cotton from bollworms, and cryIAb protects corn from the corn borer.
narration.kn: ಬ್ಯಾಸಿಲಸ್ ತುರಿಂಜಿಯೆನ್ಸಿಸ್ ನಿಷ್ಕ್ರಿಯ ಪ್ರೋಟಾಕ್ಸಿನ್ ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಕೀಟದ ಕ್ಷಾರೀಯ ಕರುಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಅದು ಸಕ್ರಿಯವಾಗಿ ಮಧ್ಯಕರುಳಿನ ಕೋಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ರಂಧ್ರ ಮಾಡಿ ಲಾರ್ವಾವನ್ನು ಕೊಲ್ಲುತ್ತದೆ. cryIAc ಮತ್ತು cryIIAb ಹತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಕಾಯಿಕೊರಕದಿಂದ, cryIAb ಮೆಕ್ಕೆಜೋಳವನ್ನು ಕಾಂಡಕೊರಕದಿಂದ ರಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: Bacillus thuringiensis makes a toxin that kills insects. Why does the toxin not kill the bacterium itself, and why must the insect actually eat it?

steps.en: Inside the bacterium the toxin is stored as crystals of an inactive protoxin, so it cannot harm the cell.
The protoxin is activated only by the alkaline pH of the insect gut, which solubilises the crystals.
The active toxin acts by binding to the surface of the insect's midgut epithelial cells and making pores, so it must reach the gut.

answer.en: It is an inactive protoxin inside the bacterium; it becomes active only in the alkaline insect gut, where it binds midgut cells.
